_comment: Navigation sweep profile for Mega Man 2 (ADR-0239, PRD Part A slice F14.17).
Read by scripts/record_navigation_sweep.py.
RUNG 1, NOT RUNG 2. ADR-0239 section 1 says to use the first rung that
reaches the place, and for this ROM that is rung 1: the game's own stage
select. navigation.kind is 'input', so no cheat rides with any session and
every session is an ADR-0184 section 2 clean pass that all four of
ADR-0183's surfaces may read. Rung 2 was checked and is not needed:
DataCrystal's map does publish one stage-select byte (see the RAM check
below), but the ladder stops at the first rung that reaches every place,
and this one reaches all eight.
THE SELECTOR THE GAME OFFERS. The Mega Man 2 instruction booklet (Capcom
USA, 1989; archive.org item 'mega-man-2-nes-manual', file
'Mega-Man-2-Game-Manual_djvu.txt'), 'GETTING STARTED': 'The story of Mega
Man will begin. If you would like to skip the story, press START.' ...
'Use SELECT to choose NORMAL or DIFFICULT mode. Press START to begin the
game.' ... '3. You must now choose to START or enter a PASSWORD. Press
START to begin the game.' ... '4. The STAGE SELECT screen will appear.
This screen has pictures of all eight enemy robots plus a spot in the
middle for Dr. Wiley. Use the control pad to move the flashing box to the
opponent of your choice and press START.'
Every one of those screens was also read off this ROM directly on
2026-09-26, by running the entry scripts under scripts/headless_record with
its 'screenshot' flag and stepping the run length (the probes are under
runs/f1417/megaman2/probe/, unversioned). The measured sequence, in frames
from power-on: black to ~250 (the power-on story and the title's fade-in),
the NORMAL/DIFFICULT title screen from ~360, the START/PASSWORD menu from
~420, and the eight-robot stage select from ~450. That is why each entry
script taps START eight times 30 frames apart: the console ignores a START
that arrives while a screen is still being drawn, so the taps are redundant
on purpose and the ones that land early or late cost nothing.
THE GRID, AND ITS NUMBERING. The stage select is a 3x3 grid whose centre is
Dr. Wily, and DataCrystal's map numbers the cursor clockwise from Bubble
Man (see the source line below):
Bubble 01   Air 02      Quick 03
Heat 08     Dr. Wily 00 Wood 04
Metal 07    Flash 06    Crash 05
The cursor starts on Dr. Wily, and START there does nothing until the eight
Robot Masters are beaten - measured: eight START taps with no direction
press leave the select screen exactly where it was. Each value below
therefore moves the cursor off the centre first and then presses START.
Every move was verified against the byte the map publishes, on a run that
stopped on the select screen: right reads 04, up 02, down 06, left 08, and
each value's own entry script lands on the value its title claims.
THE RAM CHECK, AND WHAT IT PROVES. $002A is 'Stage select cursor position:
$00=Dr. Wily, $01-$08 clockwise starting from Bubble Man' (DataCrystal,
Mega Man 2/RAM map, https://datacrystal.tcrf.net/wiki/Mega_Man_2/RAM_map,
read through the Wayback Machine on 2026-09-26 - the live page is behind a
Cloudflare challenge). It is the only stage byte the map publishes, and it
is the byte the stage select itself sets.
What each value's ramCheck asserts is the game's own stage id, which the
same byte carries once the stage has started. The numbering there is not
the map's cursor numbering but the game's own Robot Master order - Heat 0,
Air 1, Wood 2, Bubble 3, Quick 4, Flash 5, Metal 6, Crash 7 - and the
expectations below are MEASURED, not published: each was read with
scripts/mss_ram.py off a session's final state, and the order was checked
against all eight at once (0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7 exactly once each). A check is
not a cheat, so ADR-0184 section 5's source rule does not reach these
numbers - the same reading scripts/stages/ninjagaiden/navigation.json makes
of its own $006E. What a passing check says is that the state at the end of
the run is the stage the value's title names and not the title, the stage
select or the GAME OVER menu.
A FAILING CHECK IS NOT ALWAYS A BROKEN RUN, and on this ROM it is a
statement about the menu. Measured 2026-09-26 on the sweep's own shape with
a body that only runs right (runs/f1417/megaman2/probe/scan/, one session
per value at 40 s and at 120 s): while a session still has a life left,
the byte holds the stage id, and four of the eight did at 120 s (Quick,
Wood, Crash and Flash, the four whose bodies had not yet lost all three
lives). A session that has lost its three lives ends on the GAME OVER menu
(CONTINUE / STAGE SELECT / PASSWORD, read off the final screenshot), and
the byte then reads 05 for Bubble, Air, Metal and Heat - the same value for
all four, which is the menu's own leftover and not the stage. That is the
same case scripts/stages/excitebike/navigation.json documents for its
$004F, which returns to 00 when a race ends: read the check together with
ADR-0239 section 4's 'new' count, which is the gate.
The body this profile ships is written so that case does not arise: it
carries a START press at the end of every pass, which on the GAME OVER menu
restarts the stage through the game's own CONTINUE and costs ~20 frames of
the pause screen while the game is playing. All eight values were measured
at 120 s with it and every one ends inside its own stage.
NO LIVES PIN, AND THE INERT CONTROL WAS NOT RUN HERE. defaults.cheats is
absent, so no process in this sweep is launched with a cheat and section
3's control - which exists to test a pin - has nothing to test. It was not
run for that reason; it is NOT a claim that it passed. The pin that was
considered is the life counter, $00A8 ('Number of Lives remaining',
DataCrystal, Mega Man 2/RAM map, read through the Wayback Machine on
2026-09-26), and the argument against it is the mechanism ADR-0184 section
1 describes: a RAM cheat substitutes the byte on the CPU's read bus and
never writes memory, so the game reads a fixed value however often it
decrements and the HUD shows that value after a death where the uncheated
run shows one less - a different textures/ tree by construction, which is
the failure the control exists to catch. That control was run on both of
the two games that tried a pin and failed byte for byte on each
(docs/validation/f1416-coverage-sweep-2026-09-26.md: Castlevania 002A:04,
166 of 529 files differ; Ninja Gaiden 0076:02, 226 of 627), which is why
the F14.16 sweeps carry no pin. Nothing about this ROM differs in the
respect that matters - the counter is read by the game and drawn by the
HUD, both on the read bus - but that is an argument from the mechanism and
the precedent, not a measurement of this ROM, and this profile does not
claim one. The deaths, the respawns and the GAME OVER menu stay on the
record, which is what ADR-0184 section 4 asks for.
CAVEAT THAT APPLIES TO EVERY SESSION. The selector is input and the body
never clears a stage, so no session records a stage-clear transition
(ADR-0184's 2026-09-14 amendment, ADR-0239 section 6): the Robot Master's
room and the weapon-get screen are reached only by beating a stage, which
is rung 3 work a later measurement has to name. What the sweep does reach
is each stage, its enemies, its background and its GAME OVER menu.

navigation.source: The Mega Man 2 instruction booklet (Capcom USA, 1989), 'GETTING STARTED' steps 2-4: SELECT chooses NORMAL or DIFFICULT on the title screen, START begins the game, the next screen is 'to START or enter a PASSWORD', and 'The STAGE SELECT screen will appear. This screen has pictures of all eight enemy robots plus a spot in the middle for Dr. Wiley. Use the control pad to move the flashing box to the opponent of your choice and press START.' (archive.org item 'mega-man-2-nes-manual', file 'Mega-Man-2-Game-Manual_djvu.txt', read 2026-09-26.) Corroborated screen by screen off this ROM's own output on 2026-09-26, and by DataCrystal's 'Mega Man 2/RAM map' for the cursor's numbering. ADR-0239 section 1 rung 1: input, no cheat.

_defaultsComment: The entry is mint-stage1.txt, which is Bubble Man's path and therefore the
game's own first stage - the same shape scripts/stages/excitebike uses,
where defaults.entry is the track-1 mint and the matching value does not
name its own. It is also the only entry scripts/library_job.py can mint a
state from, so the unattended job can record the stage-1 route.
The body is one blind pass of run-right / jump / shoot, 738 frames, and
record_navigation_sweep.py repeats it until the 120 s budget is covered
(ADR-0239 section 6). It never reads an enemy and never aims, so Mega Man
dies on most stages and loses his three lives inside the run; the deaths
and respawns are recorded, which is what ADR-0184 section 4 asks for. Each
pass ends with two short START presses: on the GAME OVER menu the first one
picks CONTINUE and puts the run back in its own stage, and the second is
what keeps the pair inert while the game is playing (the pause is a toggle
on the press, so a single press would leave the game paused for the whole
following pass - measured: the same body with one START per pass ends the
run on the password screen instead of the stage).
